name: Modern Paganism and Wicca
line: Modern Pagans, including Wiccans, follow nature-centered paths inspired by the old religions of Europe and nearby lands.
summary: Modern Paganism is a family of new religions that grew in the late 1800s and 1900s. They draw on the old, pre-Christian religions of Europe, North Africa and West Asia. Wicca, Druidry and Heathenry are some of these paths. Pagans share a love for nature and honor the cycle of life and death. Many honor a Goddess and a God, or many gods, and some see the divine in all of nature. Most Pagans do not follow a fixed creed. Many follow a simple rule: do what you will, as long as it harms none. Pagans mark the seasons with eight yearly holidays, and many meet at the full moon. Some practice alone; others meet in small groups called covens.
beliefs: Nature is sacred, and people are kin to all living things.
The divine may be a Goddess and a God, many gods, or present in all nature.
Each person is responsible for their own choices: harm none.
Life and death move in a cycle that keeps renewing.
There is no single holy book or creed, so views differ.
practices: Celebrating eight seasonal holidays, including the solstices.
Meeting for ritual at the full moon.
Practicing alone, or with a small group such as a coven.
Rituals outdoors or at a home altar, with symbols and meditation.
Marking life events, like handfasting, a Pagan wedding.
